text:
Maya Patel: Quick q — we need to decide behavior when a canary triggers a sustained token-cost spike. If token spend > 120% of baseline for 5m, do we autopause the rollout or divert traffic to a cheaper model variant? trying to weigh cost vs user-facing errors.

Jason Wu: My vote is divert to a compatible cheaper variant where possible. autopause is noisy for apps. :thinking_face:

Liam O'Connor: We have fallbacks for availability, but cost-based routing is new. divert requires verifying the cheaper variant is functionally compatible (schema, semantics). risk of subtle regressions in outputs.

Anika Reddy: From console UX, autopause is fine if operators get an explicit banner + a labeled "resume" button and clear audit log. silent diversion needs a visible badge on the route and an explanation for affected customers.

Maya Patel: Good point. We should also consider partial diversion (e.g., 50% divert, 50% keep) as a middle ground before full autopause. Any metric suggestions to drive this?

Jason Wu: Add a metric: canary_token_rate_ratio = canary_tokens_per_min / baseline_tokens_per_min. Alert if >1.2 for 5m. Rollout controller can act on that signal.

Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Implementation notes: the controller needs an ordered action list: 
```
policy:
  trigger: cost_threshold
  window: 5m
  threshold: 1.2
  actions:
    - type: partial_divert
      percent: 50
      target: model:base-quant-v2
    - type: pause
      grace: 10m
```
We'd need compatibility metadata in model registry for automatic mapping.

Anika Reddy: UX: show a time-series of canary_token_rate_ratio on the rollout detail page, plus a small explainer tooltip: "Partial divert routes X% of traffic to target model to protect stability/costs." Also surface examples of changed outputs (diff view) for operators.

Jason Wu: Also be mindful of bursty token patterns from a single tenant. Need per-tenant and per-route aggregation, not just global canary-level. Otherwise a noisy tenant could trigger autopause for everyone.

Maya Patel: Yes — require scope in the policy: scope: [tenant, route, global]. Default: route.

Liam O'Connor: ops-bot can run a replay job to validate the cheaper variant on recent prompts before diverting. If replay failure rate > 5% within validation window, skip divert and notify.

ops-bot: replay-check scheduled: job/rcp-1976 queued, will report pass/fail in #eng-platform when complete. :robot_face:

Jason Wu: Implementation plan: I'll prototype the partial_divert action in the controller this week (simple weighted routing change). Need an endpoint from registry: GET /models/{id}/compatibility -> {ok: bool, reasons: []}.

Liam O'Connor: I'll add canary_token_rate_ratio to telemetry + per-tenant breakdown, and a short alert runbook for oncall.

Anika Reddy: I'll mock the UX states (normal, partial diverted, paused) and draft copy for the banners and audit entries.

Maya Patel: Nice. Let's treat default policy as: 5m window, 1.2 threshold -> 50% partial_divert -> 10m pause if still >1.2. Schedule a 30min sync Fri 10am to review prototype + replay results. :calendar:

Jason Wu: +1. I'll link PR when ready. :thumbsup:

Liam O'Connor: +1 — adding runbook notes now.

Anika Reddy: +1 — will post mocks ahead of sync.

Maya Patel: Thanks team — closing thread for now.
